chunks: And by this chain, it was said: Three [groups] against whom argument is made

the mute, the child, and the one who died during the period [of prophethood], so a fire is raised for them and it is said to them: Enter it. So whoever enters it, it becomes for him a coolness and peace
and whoever refuses, the Blessed and High says: 'This I commanded you, but you disobeyed Me.'

key_terms.الْفَتْرَة: The period between two prophets when no prophet was present
key_terms.بَرْداً وَ سَلَاماً: Coolness and peace (a state of ease and acceptance)
key_terms.يُحْتَجُّ عَلَيْهِم: Argument is made against them / They are held accountable

ai.seo_question: Who are the three groups that will be argued against on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the eschatological status of the mute, children, and those who died during the *fatrah* (gap between prophets), emphasizing that their entry into Hell is a test of obedience rather than a punishment for inherent guilt. The narrative illustrates the concept of *baradan wa salaman* (coolness and peace) for those who willingly submit to God's command, mirroring Abraham's experience, while highlighting the divine justice for those who refuse despite having no prior obligation.
